links.outcome: Correlation between ChatGPT-5 self-declared confidence (1-5) and answer correctness on exam questions
links.effect: Correctness was positively correlated with self-assessed confidence (p = 0.029); confidence differences between clinical and theoretical questions were not significant (Mann-Whitney p = 0.07).
links.quote: Answer correctness was positively correlated with the model's self-assessed confidence level (p = 0.029): the higher the declared confidence, the greater the likelihood of a correct response.

screen.reason: The study benchmarks the performance of ChatGPT on a medical specialty examination (Polish PES in Balneology and Physical Medicine) and evaluates its self-assessed confidence, without testing any organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
